newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on ailing peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on ailing peso.

text.p: Overnight Cetes rates closed 90 basis points higher at 29.50 percent on Wednesday, primarily due to peso weakness, traders said.
Early highs were reined in somewhat by a large buyer stepping in towards the close.

Rates had risen to a high of 32.75 percent as the peso floundered against the dollar and liquidity was squeezed by the cutoff on Wednesday for banks settling outstanding balances on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
"It was a very tough day. On top of the central bank's cutoff date, we had demand for month-end liquidity and the peso failing to respond to primary hikes," a trader said.
Earlier, the benchmark 48-hour peso ended at its weakest ever closing rate, at 7.9850/8.0050, or 6.5 centavos off Tuesday's close.
Traders said that expectations of rising inflation in November and December were also pushing rates up.
"Wage and energy hikes will fuel inflation, and speculation on that is beginning,"a trader said.

Inflation tends to reach a seasonal spike in December, but traders noted that the Alliance for Economic Growth signed on Saturday by government, business and labor leaders provided for wage rises and hikes in energy costs.
The 28-day rate closed 100 basis points higher at 29.75 percent, compared to a current primary rate of 29.34 percent.
Local analysts pointed to seasonal factors as also being responsible for jitters.
Banco de Mexico had earlier injected 2.961 billion pesos in the secondary market.
Traders said that government spending of some 1.5 billion pesos eased a liquidity shortfall originally estimated at 3.503 billion pesos.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 45 basis points up at 31.40 percent.
Total credit maturities for Thursday were estimated at 987 million pesos.
